content.text:
**Finding: COMPLIANT — no redline proposed.**

The licence grant runs in our favour (AbbVie is licensee) and satisfies the preferred checklist on its material terms:

- **Affiliates / contractors** — Section 5.3 gives us an unconditional right to sublicense through multiple tiers "to its Affiliates and other Persons" (no consent, only a post-execution copy); Sections 5.4, 5.5 and 13.16 reinforce Affiliate rights. This exceeds the fallback's "on written notice".
- **Successor transfer** — Section 13.4.1 permits assignment without consent to a successor in a merger, sale of stock or sale of assets, meeting both the fallback M&A transfer and the preferred successor element.
- **Not revocable at will** — Harpoon can terminate only for uncured material breach (12.2.1, 90-day cure; 12.2.2 diligence) or insolvency (12.4); there is no discretionary revocation, so we are well clear of walk-away territory.
- **Paid-up perpetual/irrevocable** — Section 12.1.2 makes the Section 5.1.3 grants "non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable" on expiry of the Term.

Noted in the rationale rather than flagged: the insolvency termination trigger, and that post-expiry irrevocability converts the grant to non-exclusive and covers only the 5.1.3 licences. These are customary here and not material fallback failures.
